title: The volume of a flanged hub
statement: A flanged hub is a flange of diameter $80\ \text{mm}$ and thickness $10\ \text{mm}$, with a hub of diameter $40\ \text{mm}$ standing on it to an overall height of $30\ \text{mm}$. A bore of diameter $20\ \text{mm}$ runs through both, and four bolt holes of diameter $8\ \text{mm}$ pass through the flange. Find the volume of the hub.
given: four bolt holes $\varnothing 8\ \text{mm}$ through the flange

artefact.caption: Each primitive's volume $V = \frac{\pi}{4} d^2 l$, added or taken away

steps.title: Split it into primitives
steps.note: The hub is two cylinders that add (the flange, and the hub standing on it) and two kinds of hole that take away (the bore through both, and the bolt holes through the flange). None of them overlaps another, so their volumes add and subtract exactly. The hub stands $30 - 10 = 20\ \text{mm}$ above the flange.

steps.title: The cylinders that add
steps.note: Each cylinder's volume is $V = \frac{\pi}{4} d^2 l$: the flange gives $50265.5\ \text{mm}^3$ and the hub $25132.7\ \text{mm}^3$.

steps.title: The holes that take away
steps.note: The bore runs the full height, $9424.8\ \text{mm}^3$; each bolt hole is $502.7\ \text{mm}^3$, four of them $2010.6\ \text{mm}^3$. Both are taken away.

steps.title: Add them up
steps.note: The cylinders give $50265.5 + 25132.7$; less the holes' $9424.8$ and $2010.6$, that leaves $V = 63962.8\ \text{mm}^3$.
